payload.prompt: What does an analyzer do?

options.text: Analyzes input and returns structured results
options.rationale: An analyzer accepts content and applies AI analysis. It returns structured results.

options.text: Defines only the fields to extract
options.rationale: A schema defines fields and structure. An analyzer performs the analysis.
options.better_fit: This describes a schema used to define requested fields.

options.rationale: Storage happens after analysis returns results. It is not the analyzer's role.
options.better_fit: This fits a downstream system that saves returned JSON.

options.rationale: Data types may appear in a result. An analyzer does more than report metadata.
options.better_fit: This fits a description of typed result fields.

payload.feedback_for_correct: Correct. An analyzers accepts content, applies analysis, and returns structured output.

payload.prompt: Which are roles of an analyzer? Select all that apply.

options.rationale: An analyzer applies AI analysis to submitted content. This is its central role.
Analyzers return structured results. Those results support later workflows.
A configured analyzer reuses its extraction logic and schema. This makes output predictable.

options.text: Creates a new schema for every request
options.rationale: Analyzers reuse their configured schema for similar inputs. New schemas per request reduce consistency.
options.better_fit: This may be needed when requirements genuinely change.

payload.feedback_for_correct: Correct. Analyzers analyze input, return structured results, and reuse configured logic.

payload.prompt: Evaluate this statement.
payload.statement: A configured analyzer can reuse the same schema for every analysis request.
payload.feedback_for_correct: Correct. Schema reuse makes repeated results predictable.

feedback_for_incorrect.intrinsic: Similar inputs could produce inconsistent field structures.
feedback_for_incorrect.instructional: A configured analyzer consistently reuses its extraction logic and schema.

payload.prompt: The reusable configuration that specifies which fields an analyzer should extract is a ___.

parts.text: The reusable configuration that specifies which fields an analyzer should extract is a

payload.explanation: A schema specifies fields and structure for extraction.

feedback_for_incorrect.intrinsic: The requested field structure would remain undefined.
feedback_for_incorrect.instructional: A schema defines fields; an analyzer performs analysis.

payload.prompt: Arrange the steps for reusing one analyzer on a submitted receipt.
payload.explanation: Select the analyzer, submit content, apply its schema, then receive structured JSON.

feedback_for_incorrect.intrinsic: A result would be placed before the analysis that produces it.
feedback_for_incorrect.instructional: Follow the dependency from analyzer selection through returned JSON.

payload.prompt: An expense team receives thousands of receipts and needs the same fields from every one. Which approach should it choose?

options.text: Reuse one configured analyzer and schema
options.rationale: One configured analyzer applies the same logic and schema to every receipt. This produces comparable results.

options.text: Create a different schema for each receipt
options.rationale: The team needs common fields across receipts. Different schemas would make outputs inconsistent.
options.better_fit: Use this when different content types require different fields.

feedback.intrinsic: Expense values would be harder to compare.
feedback.instructional: Stable requirements call for one reused analyzer and schema.

options.text: Use basic OCR without a schema
options.rationale: OCR can return text without the required named-field structure. The task needs repeatable extraction.
options.better_fit: Use this when only page text is needed.

feedback.intrinsic: Receipt text may lack consistent expense fields.
feedback.instructional: Use an analyzer and schema for repeated named-field extraction.

options.rationale: Confidence is returned after a field is extracted. It cannot define the extraction workflow.
options.better_fit: Use this after analysis to assess a returned field.

feedback.intrinsic: There would be no extracted value to assess.
feedback.instructional: Confidence is result metadata, not an extraction configuration.

payload.feedback_for_correct: Correct. Reuse provides consistent extraction.

payload.prompt: Which are listed prebuilt analyzer IDs? Select all that apply.

options.rationale: prebuilt-invoice is a supplied analyzer ID. It fits invoice analysis.
prebuilt-imageSearch is a listed prebuilt ID. It is supplied for a common scenario.
prebuilt-audioSearch is a listed prebuilt ID. It supports audio analysis.
custom-invoice is not a listed prebuilt ID. Custom analyzers are tailored by users.
options.better_fit: This could be a user-created analyzer name.

payload.feedback_for_correct: Correct. These are supplied IDs for common scenarios.

payload.prompt: True or false?
payload.statement: A custom analyzer is supplied for a common scenario without tailoring it to your requirements.
payload.feedback_for_correct: Correct. That describes a prebuilt analyzer.

feedback_for_incorrect.instructional: Custom analyzers are tailored to requirements and schema.

payload.prompt: Decide whether this statement is true or false.
payload.statement: A prebuilt analyzer can be selected when a supplied common scenario matches the required extraction task.
payload.feedback_for_correct: Correct. Prebuilt analyzers are supplied for common scenarios.

feedback_for_incorrect.intrinsic: A ready-made option could be overlooked.
feedback_for_incorrect.instructional: Choose prebuilt when its scenario fits; choose custom when tailoring is needed.

payload.prompt: Arrange the phrase that distinguishes a custom analyzer.
payload.explanation: Custom analyzers are tailored to a user's extraction requirements and schema.

feedback_for_incorrect.intrinsic: The custom-versus-prebuilt distinction would be unclear.
feedback_for_incorrect.instructional: Keep the tailoring relationship together in the completed statement.

payload.prompt: An analyzer supplied for a common scenario is a ___.

parts.text: An analyzer supplied for a common scenario is a

payload.explanation: A prebuilt analyzer is supplied for a common scenario.

feedback_for_incorrect.intrinsic: A tailored option could be confused with a supplied one.
feedback_for_incorrect.instructional: Use prebuilt for a ready common-scenario analyzer.

payload.prompt: A clerk must extract fields from standard invoices today. Which choices fit? Select all that apply.

options.rationale: prebuilt-invoice is supplied for invoices. Standard invoices match its scenario.
A prebuilt analyzer fits a supplied common scenario. Standard invoice extraction is such a scenario.
Custom analyzers are for tailored requirements. The stated task already fits a supplied choice.
options.better_fit: Use this when invoice fields need organization-specific tailoring.

feedback.intrinsic: Time could be spent designing fields unnecessarily.
feedback.instructional: Start with prebuilt-invoice when the standard scenario fits.

options.rationale: prebuilt-audioSearch is for audio analysis. It does not fit invoice inputs.
options.better_fit: Use this when analyzing an audio file.

feedback.intrinsic: The selected analyzer would not fit the input.
feedback.instructional: Match the prebuilt analyzer to the content type.

payload.feedback_for_correct: Correct. Standard invoices fit prebuilt-invoice.

payload.prompt: An inspection manager needs fields that no supplied analyzer covers for paper safety forms. Which choices should the manager make? Select all that apply.

options.rationale: The fields are organization-specific and uncovered. A custom analyzer can be tailored for them.

options.text: Define the required inspection fields in a schema
options.rationale: The tailored extraction needs a defined field structure. A schema supplies that definition.
An invoice analyzer targets a different common scenario. It will not match unique safety-form fields.
options.better_fit: Use this for standard invoices that fit its extraction.

feedback.intrinsic: Important safety fields may not be returned.
feedback.instructional: Unique uncovered fields indicate a custom analyzer and schema.

options.rationale: The input is paper forms, not video. The required fields are also unique.
options.better_fit: Use this for a suitable video-analysis scenario.

feedback.intrinsic: An unrelated analyzer would be selected.
feedback.instructional: Evaluate both content type and required fields.

payload.feedback_for_correct: Correct. Unique uncovered fields require a custom analyzer and schema.

payload.prompt: Where can you test an analyzer with uploaded material before coding?

options.rationale: The Foundry portal supports testing uploads and examples. It can be used before automation in code.
JSON is reviewed after analysis. It is not where testing begins.
options.better_fit: Use this to name structured output after analysis.

options.rationale: The API supports programmatic requests. The portal is the visual testing interface.
options.better_fit: Use this when automating analysis in an application.

options.rationale: An SDK client is used in application code. It is not the upload-and-test portal.
options.better_fit: Use this when implementing analysis in Python.

payload.feedback_for_correct: Correct. The portal supports testing before coding.

payload.prompt: What can you do in the Foundry portal? Select all that apply.

options.rationale: The portal accepts uploaded material for testing. This supports validation before automation.

options.text: Run an analyzer on a media file
options.rationale: The portal can select source media and run an analyzer. It supports testing media inputs.
The portal can display returned JSON. This helps review structured output.
Polling belongs to asynchronous API workflows. It is not a stated portal-testing action.
options.better_fit: Use this in code after an asynchronous API request.

payload.feedback_for_correct: Correct. The portal can upload content, run analysis, and show JSON.

payload.prompt: Is the following statement accurate?
payload.statement: The Foundry portal can test an analyzer only after the workflow is automated in code.
payload.feedback_for_correct: Correct. Portal testing occurs before code automation.

feedback_for_incorrect.intrinsic: An application could be built without checking returned fields.
feedback_for_incorrect.instructional: Use the portal to test uploads before automating extraction.

payload.prompt: Before automating extraction in code, you can test an analyzer in the new Foundry ___.

parts.text: Before automating extraction in code, you can test an analyzer in the new Foundry

payload.explanation: The Foundry portal is used to test analyzers before code automation.

feedback_for_incorrect.intrinsic: A result or coding tool would be named instead of the testing interface.
feedback_for_incorrect.instructional: Choose portal for visual analyzer testing before coding.

payload.prompt: Arrange the portal-testing steps.
payload.explanation: Select a file, run analysis, then review the returned fields and JSON.

feedback_for_incorrect.intrinsic: Results would be reviewed before analysis occurred.
feedback_for_incorrect.instructional: Start with the input, run the analyzer, then inspect outputs.

payload.prompt: Mia wants to verify expected receipt fields before building her application. What should she do first?

options.text: Upload the receipt in the Foundry portal and run the analyzer
options.rationale: The portal lets Mia test a real receipt and inspect fields before coding. This validates planned extraction.
Polling happens after an asynchronous API request. Mia needs an initial test before building code.
options.better_fit: Use this when an application awaits an API operation.

feedback.intrinsic: Mia would need an API request before polling.

options.rationale: An analyzer ID identifies the processor but does not verify fields. A receipt test is required.
options.better_fit: Use this to identify the analyzer that produced a result.

feedback.instructional: Run the analyzer and inspect returned fields.

options.text: Convert the receipt to JSON herself
options.rationale: The receipt is submitted as content and analysis returns JSON. Conversion does not test the analyzer.
options.better_fit: Use JSON when reviewing returned analysis output.

feedback.intrinsic: An unnecessary conversion would delay testing.
feedback.instructional: Upload the receipt directly in the portal.

payload.feedback_for_correct: Correct. Portal testing validates fields before development.

payload.prompt: What can a document image result in the portal include? Select all that apply.

options.rationale: A document image result can include recognized text. This makes page content available for review.
A result can include layout information. Layout describes page text arrangement.
Fields can be mapped to extracted values. This connects a field name with its value.
Audio transcripts concern analyzed audio. Document images can return text, layout, and mapped fields.
options.better_fit: Use this when reviewing audio-analysis output.

payload.feedback_for_correct: Correct. Document output can show text, layout, and mapped values.

payload.prompt: What does text layout information describe?

options.text: How text is arranged on a page
options.rationale: Text layout describes the arrangement of text on a page. It helps identify where content appears.

options.text: How confident a field value is
options.rationale: Confidence measures certainty in an extracted value. It does not describe page arrangement.
options.better_fit: Use this when interpreting a confidence score.

options.rationale: An analyzer ID identifies the analyzer used. Layout describes text placement.
options.better_fit: Use this when identifying an analyzer ID.

options.text: How an audio call was spoken
options.rationale: Speech concerns audio analysis. Text layout concerns document pages.
options.better_fit: Use this when discussing an audio recording.

payload.feedback_for_correct: Correct. Layout information describes page text arrangement.

payload.prompt: Evaluate this statement.
payload.statement: The portal can map a field such as Vendor address to its extracted value.
payload.feedback_for_correct: Correct. A result can show a field and its mapped value.

feedback_for_incorrect.intrinsic: The link between a field and its value could be missed.
feedback_for_incorrect.instructional: Document analysis can map fields such as Vendor address to extracted values.

payload.prompt: Arrange the field-mapping statement.
payload.explanation: The portal can display a field such as Vendor address mapped to its extracted value.

feedback_for_incorrect.intrinsic: The field and its value would not be connected clearly.
feedback_for_incorrect.instructional: State the portal action first, then the field and mapped value.

payload.prompt: Information about how document text is arranged on a page is called text ___.

parts.text: Information about how document text is arranged on a page is called text

payload.explanation: Text layout information concerns how text is arranged on a page.

feedback_for_incorrect.intrinsic: Page arrangement would be confused with another output detail.
feedback_for_incorrect.instructional: Use layout for the arrangement of text on a document page.

payload.prompt: Leo is validating a scanned invoice and must confirm both the vendor-address value and its location on the page. Which outputs should he review? Select all that apply.

options.rationale: The mapped field shows the address value associated with its field name. It verifies the field-value pairing.
Document text lets Leo verify the recognized address content. It supports checking the extracted wording.
Layout information helps verify where the address appeared. This addresses the location requirement.
Confidence indicates certainty but not location or field mapping. Leo needs document outputs for both checks.
options.better_fit: Use this when assessing certainty in an extracted value.

feedback.intrinsic: The address location and mapping would remain unverified.
feedback.instructional: Review mapped fields, document text, and layout information.

payload.feedback_for_correct: Correct. Those outputs connect the address field, value, and page position.

payload.prompt: What does a confidence score show for an extracted field value?

options.rationale: A confidence score indicates service certainty in an extracted value. It expresses confidence for that result.
An analyzer ID identifies the analyzer used. It does not measure certainty.
options.better_fit: Use this when identifying the producing analyzer.

options.text: How text is arranged on a page
options.rationale: Text layout describes page arrangement. Confidence measures value certainty.
options.better_fit: Use this when reviewing document layout.

options.rationale: A schema defines fields before analysis. Confidence is returned for extracted values.
options.better_fit: Use this when describing extraction requirements.

payload.feedback_for_correct: Correct. Confidence measures service certainty in an extracted value.

payload.prompt: Which details can an extraction result include? Select all that apply.

options.rationale: An extraction result can include an analyzer ID. It identifies the analyzer used.
An extraction result can include API-version metadata. It is a returned result detail.
Returned fields can include data types such as string or date. These help interpret values.
Configuration is created before analysis. It is not returned result metadata.
options.better_fit: Use this when creating or tailoring an analyzer.

payload.feedback_for_correct: Correct. Results can include metadata and typed field details.

payload.prompt: True or false?
payload.statement: A confidence score tells how text is arranged on a page.
payload.feedback_for_correct: Correct. Layout describes arrangement; confidence describes certainty.

feedback_for_incorrect.intrinsic: A certainty measure would be used for the wrong purpose.
feedback_for_incorrect.instructional: Confidence applies to values, while layout applies to page text.

payload.prompt: The returned result detail that identifies which analyzer produced an extraction is the ___.

parts.text: The returned result detail that identifies which analyzer produced an extraction is the

feedback_for_incorrect.intrinsic: The producing analyzer would not be identified.

payload.prompt: Nora compares results from two configured analyzers and must determine which one produced a particular extraction. Which result detail should she check?

options.rationale: The analyzer ID identifies the analyzer that produced the result. It directly supports Nora's comparison.
Confidence indicates certainty in a field value. It does not identify the producing analyzer.
options.better_fit: Use this when judging certainty in an extracted field.

feedback.intrinsic: Nora could see certainty without identifying the producer.
feedback.instructional: Check analyzer ID for source identity.

options.rationale: API version identifies an interface version, not the producing analyzer. Multiple analyzers can use one API version.
options.better_fit: Use this when identifying returned API metadata.

feedback.intrinsic: The interface version would be known, not the analyzer.
feedback.instructional: Analyzer ID names the producing analyzer.

options.rationale: Markdown can contain returned content but does not identify the analyzer reliably. The analyzer ID is explicit metadata.
options.better_fit: Use this when reviewing returned markdown content.

feedback.intrinsic: Nora might inspect content without learning its source.
feedback.instructional: Use analyzer ID to identify the producing analyzer.

payload.feedback_for_correct: Correct. The analyzer ID identifies which analyzer produced the result.

When extraction requirements and schema need tailoring.
To validate analyzer fields before automating in code.
How confident the service is in an extracted field value.
